nodes.label: Spec-Driven Schema (proposal to specs to design to tasks)
Telemetry Scan CI Workflow
nodes.rationale: First CI workflow in the repo; deliberately narrow (drives one seeded flow through the compose stack rather than running the unit suite). Run as a separate job rather than a step in a unit-test job so a slow, stack-dependent check does not slow the fast feedback loop and its failure stays legible on its own. --dry-run runs first, unconditionally, with no stack and under a second, to prove the scan's checkers still catch a planted leak before trusting a 'clean' result. Merge-vs-release gating is deliberately unsettled: design.md's Open Questions assumes merge-blocking, but the decision needs a real runtime figure first, so the 'Record scan runtime' step exists to produce that figure and the workflow currently only reports on pull requests rather than blocking them.

nodes.label: README.md — NER Platform Service & API Reference
MLflow Tracking Server K8s Deployment Manifest
AC Verification Policy (AGENTS.md Invariant 2)
nodes.rationale: Every Acceptance Criterion in any spec.md must have at least one executable verification artifact that fails when the AC's THEN clause is violated, per docs/workflow/acceptance-criteria.md.

nodes.label: Privacy boundary: LLM sees schema, never raw data
nodes.rationale: Every structured-data engagement (Gordian, FinFrock, Axiom) independently converged on the same architecture so a tenant's raw dataset is never sent to the LLM, only schema/column descriptions/metadata; the model generates an operation (SQL or Pandas expression) that a deterministic runtime executes against the real data outside the model. Valuable commercially, not just technically: it lets InApp tell a client 'your dataset is not passed to the LLM.'

nodes.label: Generate-then-execute pattern
nodes.rationale: Gordian (Pandas), FinFrock (SQL) and Axiom (SQL) all have the model emit a program rather than an answer; a deterministic runtime produces the number. Chosen because it eliminates arithmetic hallucination and makes every answer reproducible and auditable.

nodes.label: Schema metadata catalogue gap (Phase 1.1)
nodes.rationale: WHITELISTED_TABLES is a hardcoded Python dict of bare column names with no descriptions, relationships, per-tenant indexing, or search — identified as the single biggest structural gap versus Axiom's per-tenant indexed schema catalogue approach, and named as the highest-leverage fix because it unblocks confidence scoring, tabular ingestion, and the external-database connector.

nodes.label: Axiom engagement (multi-tenant schema-aware SQL at scale)
External tenant database connector (Phase 3.3)
nodes.rationale: Generalise the SQL path into a connector pointing at a tenant's own database rather than only the platform schema. Highest ceiling and largest security surface in the set, deliberately gated to start only after the schema metadata catalogue (1.1) and query validation/confidence scoring (1.2) are proven in production on the platform's own schema.

nodes.label: Integration plan (Phase 1/2/3 ordering)
nodes.rationale: Ordered by (value x fit with what the platform already has) / effort, so each item plugs into an existing seam (ToolRegistry, pending_clarification, SQL path) rather than requiring the chat graph to be re-architected.

nodes.label: Six chained bugs: extraction silently used base model
nodes.rationale: S3 artifact path mismatch, label_list never persisted, hardcoded port pointing to host-mapped training_service:8003 instead of Docker-internal :8000, missing NER_MODEL_SERVING_URL env var, ONNX input mismatch (token_type_ids sent but not declared), and a too-tight 30s warmup timeout all independently caused inference to fall back to the base model silently, because graceful-degradation fallback code masked every one of them instead of surfacing an error.

nodes.label: Open bug: eval F1/precision/recall = 0.0 on model v8
ADR-001: Tenant Data Isolation via Separate Database Schemas
nodes.rationale: Chose separate PostgreSQL schema per tenant (tenant_<uuid>) over (a) separate database per tenant (strongest isolation but high per-database operational cost) and (c) shared tables with row-level security (lowest overhead but highest misconfiguration/leakage risk). Schema-per-tenant gives strong logical isolation without per-database overhead, single migration script set, and single connection pool, at the cost of a shared-fate single PostgreSQL instance and linear schema-count scaling requiring sharding above ~500 tenants.

nodes.label: ADR-002: Single Curated Base Model Strategy (No BYOM)
nodes.rationale: Chose a single curated base model (dslim/bert-base-NER) for every tenant over (b) a curated multi-model list or (c) full bring-your-own-model, to eliminate the model compatibility matrix, keep a single ONNX export/optimization path, and make cross-tenant metric comparisons meaningful because baselines are identical — at the cost of blocking tenants with existing fine-tuned models and requiring re-fine-tuning all tenants on any base model upgrade.

nodes.label: ADR-003: Per-Tenant Model Serving Topology (Shared Pool + Routing)
nodes.rationale: Chose a shared Model Serving Layer with per-tenant routing and version pinning (with a path to dedicated pods for high-volume tenants) over (a) a dedicated inference pod per tenant (strongest isolation, high cost for low-volume tenants) and (c) serverless per-request inference (lowest cost but multi-minute cold-start latency), to amortize GPU utilization across tenants while accepting a noisy-neighbor risk mitigated by per-tenant rate limiting, QoS weights, and dedicated-pod escalation.

nodes.label: ADR-004: OpenSpec Spec-Driven Development Governance
nodes.rationale: Adopted OpenSpec SDD with mandatory proposal/design/spec/tasks/evidence/archive gates over (a) ad-hoc documentation (no traceability enforcement) and (c) fully formalized specification with formal verification (unsustainable overhead), because the project mandates AI-native delivery traceable from business intent through implementation evidence across multiple concurrent human and agent contributors; a documented exception list keeps trivial changes low-overhead.

nodes.label: ADR-005: OpenCode Agent Permissions and Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Chose role-specific agents with bounded tool access and human approval gates over (a) a single general-purpose agent (high risk of unintended cross-domain actions) and (c) a fully automated agent pipeline (fastest but highest risk), to prevent e.g. a coding agent from modifying infrastructure config or a QA agent deploying to production, at the cost of more agent handoffs for simple changes.

nodes.label: ADR-006: Training Infrastructure with Asynchronous GPU Workers
nodes.rationale: Chose a hybrid of (b) Celery-based async GPU workers with a RabbitMQ broker and (c) dedicated K8s Job per training run, backed by GPU node pools that autoscale 0->N, over (a) synchronous training in the API process (unacceptable — blocks the API), so training never blocks the API/extraction path while getting mature task management, retries, and per-job monitoring; checkpointing enables resume from failure.

nodes.label: ADR-007: Chatbot Architecture with Full RAG and Guardrails
nodes.rationale: Chose a full RAG pipeline combining SQL over extracted entities, pgvector semantic/full-text document search, and real-time NER inference, over (a) pure SQL generation (lacks document context/NER) and (c) a fine-tuned LLM per tenant (prohibitive cost/complexity), to deliver rich, citable answers within a P95<10s target; guardrails include SQL validation in read-only transactions, mandatory source citation, and query complexity limits.

nodes.label: ADR-008: Base Model as Default Inference Model (Version 0)
nodes.rationale: Treats dslim/bert-base-NER as a synthetic 'version 0' for every tenant so extraction requests never 404 before a tenant completes annotation->training->promotion; chosen over leaving the prior 404/400 behavior in place, which rendered the platform unusable until first promotion. Cost: base-model predictions only cover CoNLL labels, not tenant-specific ones, until a fine-tuned version is promoted.

nodes.label: ADR-009: System Admin Sets Training Hyperparameters at Approval
nodes.rationale: Moved hyperparameter selection (learning_rate, num_epochs, batch_size, max_seq_length) from Tenant Admin submission time to System Admin approval time, because under ADR-006's original design the System Admin approval was a rubber-stamp enqueuing whatever the tenant chose, putting GPU-cost- and model-quality-sensitive decisions in the hands of a role without cluster-capacity or training-best-practice visibility. Cost: approval is no longer single-click; requires filling four fields per job.

nodes.label: ADR-010: Dataset Readiness Measured Per Entity Type
nodes.rationale: Replaced ADR-006's self-contradictory 500-entity-total threshold (stated once as tenant-wide, once as per-type, and never actually enforced since NER_MIN_TRAINING_ENTITIES defaulted to 0) with a per-entity-type threshold of 200, evaluated over the union of active entity_definitions and spanned types, capped at 100% per type before averaging — because a tenant-wide total is a poor proxy for trainability: NER quality is bounded by the weakest label, and a tenant with 500 spans concentrated in one type showed 5% dashboard readiness while five configured types had zero spans and were invisible entirely.

nodes.label: ADR-011: Tenant-Scoped Azure Connection Control Plane
nodes.rationale: Extends the existing integration-profile control plane with tenant-bound lifecycle records in the public schema for Azure Blob and Azure PostgreSQL only, storing secret references (Vault-resolved outside local Compose) and non-sensitive metadata rather than (per Alternatives Considered) developer-managed profiles (can't meet self-service requirements), plaintext credential/config storage (violates secret-management controls), or arbitrary provider/connection-string input (cannot be safely validated as a finite catalog). Requires TLS, least-privilege read-only credentials, and a passing safe connection test plus governance approval before activation.

nodes.label: ADR-012: Durable Azure Blob Source Synchronization
nodes.rationale: Uses a contained Azure Blob runtime plus Celery/RabbitMQ source-sync jobs with a tenant-bound object/version ledger and lease for idempotency, over (per Alternatives Considered) keeping in-process asyncio dispatch (loses scheduled work on restart, no durable catch-up) or building Azure-specific OCR/chunking/extraction paths (duplicates the common pipeline) or persisting Blob originals durably in MinIO (violates source-only retention) — so manual, 15-minute scheduled, retry, and missed-schedule catch-up synchronization all share one durable, observable job that reuses existing NormalizedDocument/DocumentIngestionService ingestion and deletes temporary Blob bytes on every terminal path.

nodes.label: ADR-013: Contract-Governed External PostgreSQL Chat
nodes.rationale: Introduces a separate tenant-bound external-query capability validating a versioned canonical JSON schema contract and join graph, with a live schema fingerprint checked before every query and blocking on drift, executed as one AST-validated parameterized SELECT under a Vault-held least-privilege read-only role with a row cap and 10s timeout — chosen over (per Alternatives Considered) copying business rows into platform storage (violates no-copy requirement), using vector similarity to authorize schema (not deterministic authorization), reusing the platform SQL whitelist unchanged (doesn't represent customer schema/credentials), or permitting unrestricted read-only SQL (can still expose unauthorized data or exhaust resources). The LLM never holds database credentials and result rows are never persisted.

nodes.label: ADR-014: Local Docker Compose Deployment Topology
External Data Source Architecture (Keka-first sync engine)
Multi-tenant NER Platform investor/exec deck (scroll-snap slide deck)
Presenter Script for Multi-Tenant NER Platform deck
Deployment Plan — Tenant Self-Service Data Sources (dev-only Compose)
Mockup: Data Source Connection detail screen (HTML)
Technical Design: Tenant Self-Service Data Sources
UI Design Contract — Tenant Self-Service Data Sources
UI Inventory — Tenant Self-Service Data Sources (SCR-1/2/3, CMP-1..10)
DocumentIngestionService (inbound port)
nodes.rationale: Single application use-case every adapter (upload, Keka, S3, Azure) calls; owns identity, validation, checksum, dedup, retention decision, row write, and dispatch, so provider knowledge never leaks past the seam.

nodes.label: DocumentContent (re-openable byte access port)
nodes.rationale: open() must be re-openable, not a one-shot buffer, so a non-retained document can still be reprocessed by re-fetching from its source instead of making platform retention mandatory and quietly defeating the privacy requirement.

nodes.label: OriginalDocumentStore (outbound blob-storage port)
nodes.rationale: storage_reference must become an outcome (nullable) rather than an input the route invents, and nothing downstream may parse it, so 'do not copy this tenant's documents into platform MinIO' is a configuration value rather than a fork of the pipeline.

nodes.label: DocumentSource (deferred pull-side port)
nodes.rationale: Upload is a push source (bytes arrive unbidden); Keka/S3/Azure are pull sources (enumerate, decide, fetch). One interface serving both would force upload to fake discover()/check_connection(), so the pull contract is kept separate and deliberately not built yet.

nodes.label: SourceConnector (provider adapter contract: check_connection/discover/fetch)
nodes.rationale: Three methods only; sync (leasing, checkpointing, idempotency, failure isolation) stays with the engine so each provider does not reimplement it differently and wrongly.

nodes.label: external_documents identity ledger
nodes.rationale: Kept as a separate table rather than columns on documents because an external object can exist pre-ingestion, documents are soft-deleted (a unique index there would block re-ingest), sync bookkeeping is not document metadata, and content-addressed reuse makes the relationship many-to-one.

nodes.label: Change-detection ladder (version / timestamp / content-hash rungs)
nodes.rationale: Rungs are guarded on nullable capability declarations, not assumed, so a provider with no timestamps or versions (Keka) falls through to content-hash as a supported configuration rather than a degraded one.

nodes.label: CredentialProvider indirection (credential_ref resolution)
nodes.rationale: Credentials are never stored in the database, only a locator; resolution happens once per run in the engine so a connector has no API with which to ask for another tenant's secret. Satisfies AGENTS.md invariant 3 against secrets in config/database rows.

nodes.label: Five-boundary frame (document acquisition, blob, relational, vector, business-DB query)
nodes.rationale: The five boundaries are not equally worth building; treating them as five instances of the same pattern is named as the main programme risk. Document acquisition and blob storage are small, high-value ports; relational persistence should be relocated, not abstracted; vector needs a reshaped existing protocol; business-DB query is a new retrieval capability, not an adapter.

nodes.label: P3 — Derived relational persistence: connection routing, not a repository abstraction
nodes.rationale: entity_views.py generates DDL at runtime (CREATE TABLE/ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS), relational_projection.py uses ON CONFLICT/GREATEST upserts, and provisioning clones templates via pg_tables — a vendor-neutral abstraction would have to reproduce all of that per engine, which is 'a second product'; pointing the identical schema at a different PostgreSQL server is far cheaper and is the recommended path.

nodes.label: CAP-2 — Tenant-Scoped Connection Control Plane
nodes.rationale: Foundation capability; extends the existing public integration-profile seam into a tenant-admin lifecycle for exactly two approved Azure provider types, with server-side tenant capability resolution so caller-provided identifiers are never authority.

nodes.label: CAP-3 — Durable Azure Blob Synchronization and Source Reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Routes through NormalizedDocument/DocumentIngestionService rather than a second pipeline; retains Blob bytes only in temporary working storage so no durable original copy accumulates in MinIO.

nodes.label: CAP-4 — Contract-Governed External PostgreSQL Query Path
nodes.rationale: Kept distinct from platform SQL chat; a live-schema fingerprint must match the accepted contract before every query so drift blocks execution rather than silently returning wrong results.

nodes.label: CAP-5 — Tenant Data Source Administration Portal
nodes.rationale: Consumes only safe backend contracts from CAP-2 through CAP-4; never renders secrets, connection strings, provider errors, SQL, or database rows.

nodes.label: CAP-6 — Local Compose Delivery, Migration, and Operational Evidence
nodes.rationale: Makes the integrated feature locally deployable under the single approved dev Compose environment; no staging/production claim is introduced, matching ADR-014's explicit deferral of those environments.

nodes.label: Model quality (F1/precision/recall/loss) deliberately absent from every metric family
nodes.rationale: MLflow already versions model quality against the run, params and artifact; a Prometheus mirror would be a second source of truth with worse fidelity and shorter retention.

nodes.label: Entity-type label deliberately absent from every metric family
nodes.rationale: Entity types are tenant-configured; a metric label carrying them (e.g. policy_holder, claim_number) would identify a tenant's vocabulary to every dashboard user. Per-type counts live on the extraction run's span instead, which is tenant-scoped and expires with the trace (ADR-010).

skip-degraded scoring rule (previous)
nodes.rationale: Under skip-degraded, a query whose run degraded or errored was marked skipped and dropped out of the mean, so a configuration that broke on half the golden set scored the same as one that answered all of it.

nodes.label: zero-degraded scoring rule (current)
nodes.rationale: Degraded or errored queries score zero and stay in the denominator, making regressions visible instead of silently dropping out of the mean.
